name: [OPS] 10 · Monitor story health and credits
description: SKELETON — NOT A REAL EXPORT. This file lists the actions, names, types and links that /tines-build-story produces for the agentic sweep (Mode 3), with placeholder GUIDs and formula sketches, in the exact agents[] order the links depend on. The first `/tines-export ops-story-health-monitor` (GET /api/v1/stories/{id}/export?randomize_urls=false&clear_recipients=true | scripts/normalize.jq) replaces this file entirely. Never hand-edit; links reference agents by index. Every key or type marked VERIFY is unconfirmed until read from a real export (docs/VERIFY.md #8, #16, #19, #26). Design: ./DESIGN.md (§5 of the root design). Mode badge: Mode 3 — one AI Agent action in Task mode whose tools are Tines tools (Send to Story sub-stories); no MCP connection by default.

diagram_notes.content:
**[OPS] 10 · Monitor story health and credits** — Mode badge: **Mode 3** (AI Agent action, Task mode, Tines tools; no MCP connection by default — at most one, the Mode 4 ops-tools-server, never alongside the Send to Story tools).

Every 15 minutes (and daily at 06:00), and whenever the router forwards an alert, this story reads live activity, AI usage and recent runs with a read-only key, runs a deterministic pre-filter against baselines and limits, and — only for anomalous stories — hands the evidence to the `triage` agent, which PROPOSES: a finding, an alert rule, a Case/issue, a Slack thread, or a PR. A tool-less `critic` re-reads high/critical findings. Nothing changes production without a verified human approval; production writes live only in [OPS] 16 · Apply approved alert rule (sub), and a disable goes through rollback.yml's break-glass job, never a direct call.

Guards in the story, not in prompts: kill switch (ops_limits.enabled), CAS lock on ops_lock, never-touch mirror, daily run and credit caps, Slack request-signature check on every callback, approver verification against ops_responders, a secret scrub before any Slack or GitHub post, expected 422/404 excluded from errors.

Inputs: schedules · Send to Story from [OPS] 01 · Slack interactivity webhook. Credentials by name: tines_api_readonly, tines_api_ops_lock (the ops_lock CAS only), tines_api_dev_autofix (dev-team-only key; dev auto-fix), slack_bot, slack_signing_secret, github_dispatch. tines_api_ops is not in this story. Resources: ops_limits, ops_responders, ops_routing, ops_lock. Records: ops_alerts, ops_findings, ops_alert_proposals, ops_baselines, ops_credit_ledger, ops_dead_letter.

agents.name: sweep_15m
agents.description: SKELETON #0 — the 15-minute schedule entry. Emits {trigger: schedule_15m, window_minutes}. Watchdog: no events for 1800 s pages the DL (a dead monitor is itself an alert). VERIFY the schedule array shape and timezone key in a real export.

agents.name: sweep_daily
agents.description: SKELETON #1 — the 06:00 tenant-time daily sweep (credits, coverage, baselines; Monday adds the digest). Emits {trigger: schedule_daily}. Watchdog 172800 s.

agents.name: receive_from_router
agents.description: SKELETON #2 — the Send to Story entry (entry_agent_guid). [OPS] 01 · Route monitoring alerts forwards any alert with severity >= medium or count >= 3, plus tenant AI-credit, event-limit and change-control events it normalised. Payload: the ops_alerts row shape (tests/sample-event.json). path/secret assigned on import.

agents.name: slack_callback
agents.description: SKELETON #3 — Slack interactivity webhook for the approval buttons. Slack posts a form-encoded `payload` field. The body is NOT authenticated by itself: every request's Slack signature (X-Slack-Signature over the timestamp and raw body, keyed with the credential slack_signing_secret) and a 5-minute timestamp window are checked in-story by verify_slack_signature (#77) and the Trigger is_signed_callback (#78) before parse_callback (#52) runs; anything that fails stops there. Include headers stays ON so the signature headers reach the story. The URL's path and secret are never committed: scripts/normalize.jq replaces them with <assigned-on-import> on every export. After the signature, the approver is still verified against ops_responders.

agents.name: normalize
agents.description: SKELETON #4 — unifies the four entries into one shape with DEFAULT() on every field, and computes the lock value once (STORY_RUN_GUID() + '|' + NOW()) so acquire/release use the same string.

agents.name: kill_switch
agents.description: SKELETON #5 — THE KILL SWITCH. Passes only when RESOURCE.ops_limits.enabled is true. Every entry crosses this first; a false value stops the story without a lock, a call or a credit.

agents.name: is_callback
agents.description: SKELETON #6 — an approval-button click → the callback path (signature check #77 → #78, then #52…), which needs no sweep lock.

agents.name: is_sweep
agents.description: SKELETON #7 — a schedule or router trigger → take the lock. VERIFY the export rule type for 'not equal'.

agents.name: acquire_lock
agents.description: SKELETON #8 — compare-and-swap on the ops_lock Resource: POST /api/v1/global_resources/{id}/replace {key: lock, value: <run guid|now>, if_value: free}. 422 = already running (VERIFY #19: 422 carries the current value) — EXCLUDED from log_error_on_status and branched on. Credential tines_api_ops_lock — a separate key used for nothing but this compare-and-swap (with steal_lock #14 and release_lock #74); the Editor-role tines_api_ops never appears in this story. Hardened: retry_on_status [429, 500-599], retries 5, emit_failure_event Always. VERIFY export keys for retries / emit_failure_event / log_error_on_status.

agents.name: lock_acquired
agents.description: SKELETON #9 — the CAS succeeded (2xx). VERIFY the exact success status of /replace.

agents.name: lock_busy
agents.description: SKELETON #10 — another run holds the lock (422).

agents.name: is_stale_lock
agents.description: SKELETON #11 — the held lock is older than ops_limits.stale_lock_minutes (its timestamp is the part after '|' in the value the 422 returned — VERIFY #19 response shape) → treat as free and steal it.

agents.name: is_fresh_lock
agents.description: SKELETON #12 — the held lock is recent → exit quietly.

agents.name: exit_busy
agents.description: SKELETON #13 — EXIT. Already running; nothing fetched, nothing spent. A router-triggered run that lands here leaves its alert `open` in ops_alerts for the next scheduled sweep.

agents.name: steal_lock
agents.description: SKELETON #14 — replace the stale value with this run's value (if_value = the stale value, so two stealers cannot both win). Credential tines_api_ops_lock (the lock-only key). Same hardening as #8.

agents.name: live_activity
agents.description: SKELETON #15 — GET /api/v1/stories?filter=PUBLISHED&include_live_activity=true&per_page=100 with tines_api_readonly (Viewer role — VERIFY #18). Gives not_working_actions_count, pending_action_runs_count, monitor_failures, actions_with_monitoring, recipients, change_control_enabled, locked, mode per story. Paginate on large tenants (VERIFY #27). Hardened as #8.

agents.name: ai_usage_today
agents.description: SKELETON #16 — GET /api/v1/ai_usage?relative_date=today&group_by=story (readonly key). Gives credits_used, billed_cost, tokens, usage_count per story. The daily branch also calls it with group_by=team (write_credit_ledger, #68).

agents.name: recent_runs
agents.description: SKELETON #17 — GET /api/v1/stories/{id}/runs?since=<window start> for each scheduled story (readonly key), looped over the story list — VERIFY the HTTP Request loop option key. Runs have NO status field: guid, duration, start_time, end_time, action_count, event_count only; failure is derived downstream. end_time null mid-run is VERIFY #16.

agents.name: load_baselines
agents.description: SKELETON #18 — Records action: search ops_baselines for the last 7 days (all stories). VERIFY the Records action export type and search/output shape (also VERIFY in example-enrich-ip).

agents.name: load_open_alerts
agents.description: SKELETON #19 — Records action: search ops_alerts with status == open and last_seen inside 2× the window. These carry the router's per-action error counts, so the sweep never lists logs across the whole tenant.

agents.name: findings
agents.description: SKELETON #20 — THE DETERMINISTIC PRE-FILTER (DESIGN §5.6). Per published story: error count (open alerts) >= error_threshold_per_window; not_working_actions_count > 0; pending_action_runs_count > baseline × 3; monitor_failures false or recipients empty (coverage gap); credits today >= 80% / 95% of credit_budget_daily (per_story or default); run duration >= overlap_ratio × schedule interval; no events beyond 2× interval on a scheduled story; a lock older than stale_lock_minutes; Mode 4 stories with no initialize events over a window. A router-triggered run marks the named story anomalous regardless. Only anomalies reach the agent; info rows are logged (#21), never sent to the model. Formulas are sketches.

local.signals_for: =(story) → sketch: [error_threshold, not_working_actions, pending_backlog, credit_pct_of_budget, overlap, silent_source, mcp_health] evaluated against LOCAL.baselines and LOCAL.limits; router trigger adds {signal: router_alert}

payload.anomalies: =FILTER(MAP(LOCAL.stories, s → {story_id: s.id, story_name: s.name, signals: LOCAL.signals_for(s), baseline: FIND(LOCAL.baselines, story_id == s.id), budget_daily: LOCAL.budget_for(s.id), router_alert: IF(normalize.trigger == "router" AND s.id == normalize.story_id, receive_from_router.body, null)}), SIZE(signals) > 0)
payload.coverage_gaps: =FILTER(MAP(LOCAL.stories, s → {story_id: s.id, story_name: s.name, monitor_failures: s.monitor_failures, recipients_count: SIZE(DEFAULT(s.recipients, []))}), monitor_failures == false OR recipients_count == 0)
payload.credit_warnings: =FILTER(MAP(LOCAL.usage_by_story, u → {story_id: u.story_id, credits_used: u.credits_used, budget: LOCAL.budget_for(u.story_id), pct: ROUND(100 * u.credits_used / LOCAL.budget_for(u.story_id))}), pct >= LOCAL.limits.credit_alert_pct[0])

agents.name: write_info
agents.description: SKELETON #21 — Records action: one ops_findings row per sweep with severity info, category sweep_summary, agent_ran false, and the counts. A leaf: it does not continue the run.

agents.name: has_coverage_gap
agents.description: SKELETON #22 — at least one published story has monitor_failures false or no recipients.

agents.name: is_dev_auto_apply
agents.description: SKELETON #23 — ops_limits.environment == dev AND auto_apply_in_dev → fix coverage immediately so builders see the behaviour. Not the only guard: the committed ops_limits example defaults to environment prod / auto_apply_in_dev false, and the two writes below use tines_api_dev_autofix, which holds a real key only in the dev team.

agents.name: recipients_add_dev
agents.description: SKELETON #24 — DEV ONLY. POST /api/v1/stories/{id}/recipients {address: the router webhook} for each gap (loop). Credential tines_api_dev_autofix — a real key only in the dev team, so this action fails closed in prod even if ops_limits is mis-set; #23 gates it as well. The address is <<RESOURCE.ops_routing.router_recipient>>? NO — the router URL carries a secret and lives only in .env / GitHub secrets; in dev the value is set in a dev-only Resource field [BY HAND] and never exported (VERIFY that Resource contents are excluded from exports — they are by design).

agents.name: story_update_dev
agents.description: SKELETON #25 — DEV ONLY. PUT /api/v1/stories/{id} {monitor_failures: true} for each gap (loop). Credential tines_api_dev_autofix (dev-team-only key; fails closed in prod). On a change-controlled story this lands in a draft (VERIFY #7) — acceptable in dev.

agents.name: is_prod_propose
agents.description: SKELETON #26 — not dev-auto-apply → a coverage gap becomes a proposal a person approves.

agents.name: coverage_proposal
agents.description: SKELETON #27 — shapes one request per gap (explode — VERIFY the Event Transform explode mode key): kind alert_rule, type recipient or monitor_failures, rationale 'published production story without the ops router / with failure notifications off'. No model involved.

payload.rationale: =CONCAT("Published story ", gap.story_name, " has ", IF(gap.monitor_failures == false, "failure notifications off", "no monitoring recipients"), " (coverage_gap, sweep ", normalize.run_id, ")")

agents.name: has_anomaly
agents.description: SKELETON #28 — at least one story failed the pre-filter. A healthy sweep stops here: zero credits.

agents.name: each_anomaly
agents.description: SKELETON #29 — one event per anomalous story (explode — VERIFY mode key). Everything downstream runs per story: the run cap, the rejected-proposal lookup, triage, critic, verdict, the branch.

agents.name: count_agent_runs
agents.description: SKELETON #30 — Records action: count ops_findings rows today with agent_ran == true — the daily run cap's input.

agents.name: under_run_cap
agents.description: SKELETON #31 — RATE CAP. agent runs today < ops_limits.agent_runs_per_day_max AND the ops team's own credits today < credit_alert_pct[1] % of its monthly allocation / days (from ai_usage_today team rows — sketch). Both are Triggers, not prompt text.

agents.name: over_run_cap
agents.description: SKELETON #32 — the complement of #31.

agents.name: capped
agents.description: SKELETON #33 — the anomaly is recorded as capped (no agent run today); the daily digest and the Status-tab alerts surface it. Continues to release_lock.

payload.reason: agent_runs_per_day_max or ops team credit cap reached

agents.name: rejected_proposals
agents.description: SKELETON #34 — Records action: search ops_alert_proposals for this story with status rejected in the last 30 days. Injected into the triage PROMPT by the story so the agent does not repeat them — deliberately not a sixth tool.

agents.name: triage
agents.description: SKELETON #35 — THE AI AGENT ACTION (Mode 3). Task mode; instructions = agent/system-instructions.md §1; prompt assembled from each_anomaly + rejected_proposals + ops_limits; output_structure = agent/output-schema.json; five read-only Send to Story tools (agent/tools.md), Timeout Duration 20 s each; skills story-health-triage + credit-budget-analyst attached [BY HAND]; temperature 0.2; timeout 120 s (max VERIFY); retries 2; tool output truncation on. Smart model because a tool is attached. Token alerts on the Status tab: Notify 150000 / Disable action 300000 daily (monitoring.ai_monitoring_thresholds). Budget line: policies/cost-ceilings.yml agents.ops-story-health-monitor/triage. NO write tool. NO MCP connection by default (at most one, the Mode 4 ops-tools-server, never alongside).

options.prompt:
Diagnose this story.

story_id: <<each_anomaly.anomaly.story_id>>
story_name: <<each_anomaly.anomaly.story_name>>
environment: <<RESOURCE.ops_limits.environment>>
never_touch: <<RESOURCE.ops_limits.never_touch>>

signals (from the deterministic pre-filter, this sweep):
<<each_anomaly.anomaly.signals>>

router_alert (present only when the router forwarded a notification):
<<each_anomaly.anomaly.router_alert>>

baseline (ops_baselines, last 7 days):
<<each_anomaly.anomaly.baseline>>

budget: {"credit_budget_daily": <<each_anomaly.anomaly.budget_daily>>, "credit_alert_pct": <<RESOURCE.ops_limits.credit_alert_pct>>}

rejected_proposals (do not repeat these):
<<rejected_proposals.records>>
options.output_structure: <agent/output-schema.json — the full JSON Schema object, pasted by the build>

tools.name: ops_get_error_logs
tools.description: Returns the most recent error-level (level 4) logs for one Tines action … (full 3–4-sentence text in agent/tools.md). Example: {"action_id": 0, "limit": 20}.

tools.name: ops_get_story_export
tools.description: Summarises one story's configuration from its export … (agent/tools.md). Example: {"story_id": 0}.

tools.name: ops_get_live_activity
tools.description: Returns the live-activity counters for one story right now … (agent/tools.md). Example: {"story_id": 0}.

tools.name: ops_get_recent_runs
tools.description: Returns run statistics for one story since a timestamp … (agent/tools.md). Example: {"story_id": 0, "since": "2026-09-23T17:00:00Z"}.

tools.name: ops_get_ai_usage
tools.description: Returns AI credit usage for one story over a relative date … (agent/tools.md). Example: {"story_id": 0, "relative_date": "today"}.

agents.name: needs_critic
agents.description: SKELETON #36 — severity high or critical → the second reader. Branches on the schema field, never on confidence.

agents.name: skip_critic
agents.description: SKELETON #37 — low or medium → straight to verdict.

agents.name: critic
agents.description: SKELETON #38 — the tool-less second reader. Task mode, NO tools, no explicit model → the tenant's fast model (cheap by construction). instructions = agent/system-instructions.md §2; output_structure = agent/critic-output-schema.json; may only confirm or lower the severity. Token alerts Notify 50000 / Disable action 100000 daily. Budget line agents.ops-story-health-monitor/critic. No skills (tines-skills/_manifest.yaml).

options.prompt:
Finding under review:
<<triage.output>>

Rule: confirm the severity or lower it. Never raise it. Cite which evidence rows were decisive in reason.

agents.name: verdict
agents.description: SKELETON #39 — merges triage and critic and applies the NEVER-TOUCH GUARD deterministically: final_severity = the lower of the two when the critic ran; needs_human forced true on critic disagreement, severity high/critical, confidence < 0.6, category unknown, or a never-touch target; final_kind forced to none for any story in RESOURCE.ops_limits.never_touch (ids or name pattern). Emits exactly eight fields; the Triggers that follow read only final_kind, final_severity and needs_human.

payload.needs_human: =LOCAL.t.needs_human OR LOCAL.never_touch OR (LOCAL.critic_ran AND LOCAL.c.agrees == false) OR INCLUDES(["high", "critical"], LOCAL.lower_sev) OR LOCAL.t.confidence < 0.6 OR LOCAL.t.category == "unknown"

agents.name: write_finding
agents.description: SKELETON #40 — Records action: the ops_findings row for this agent run — severity, category, hypothesis, fix, kind, confidence, needs_human, critic_agrees, and from the agent event's meta: model, credits_used, tokens (exact meta paths VERIFY at build). agent_ran true (the run cap counts it).

agents.name: post_thread
agents.description: SKELETON #41 — the Slack send-message template (chat.postMessage) with credential slack_bot: every finding >= medium goes to the story's thread (channel from RESOURCE.ops_routing[slug] else default; thread_ts from the router's ops_alerts row when present), with severity, the SCRUBBED hypothesis and evidence refs (from scrub #79, never triage.output directly), and a 'needs a human' marker when verdict.needs_human. Approvals are NOT posted here — [OPS] 17 posts the Block Kit buttons. Hardened as #8.

payload.text: =CONCAT("[", UPCASE(verdict.final_severity), "] ", verdict.story_name, " — ", verdict.category, ": ", scrub.hypothesis, " Evidence: ", JOIN(MAP(scrub.evidence, e → CONCAT(e.source, ":", e.ref)), ", "), IF(verdict.needs_human, " — NEEDS A HUMAN", ""), " (finding ", verdict.finding_id, ")")

agents.name: kind_none
agents.description: SKELETON #42 — record only. → release_lock.

agents.name: kind_alert_rule
agents.description: SKELETON #43 — an alert rule proposal → a human approves → the apply sub-story.

agents.name: kind_credit_action
agents.description: SKELETON #44 — at 95% of budget: pause the costliest agent or reroute it to a custom provider — TWO different approvers (credit_action is in ops_responders.two_required_for), and [OPS] 16 lands it only as a draft + change request, never a live write. (At 80% the digest/thread summary is enough.)

agents.name: kind_disable
agents.description: SKELETON #45 — disable a story: two approvers in prod (ops_responders.two_required_for), never a never-touch entry (already forced to none in #39). The approved request is routed through the break-glass path — [OPS] 16 dispatches rollback.yml with emergency: true, whose break-glass job (two GitHub reviewers) disables the story and writes the policies/break-glass-log.md line; nothing in the tenant calls POST /disable directly.

agents.name: kind_story_config
agents.description: SKELETON #46 — a story change → a GitHub issue with the diagnosis and an exact /tines-build-story prompt; plus repository_dispatch when the option is on the auto-PR allow-list.

agents.name: shape_proposal
agents.description: SKELETON #47 — maps the agent's schema output onto [OPS] 17's input for the three approval kinds: alert_rule → {type, action_id, value} from alert_rule_proposal; disable_action → kind disable, target the story; credit_action → kind credit_action, value pause_agent|reroute_provider from proposed_change.target.

agents.name: request_approval
agents.description: SKELETON #48 — Send to Story → [OPS] 17 · Request approval (sub): writes ops_alert_proposals (pending, expires_at), re-checks never-touch and max_proposals_per_day, posts the Block Kit approval to ops_routing._approvals. Returns {approval_id, status: pending, approvers, expires_at}. Called by the STORY after a Trigger — never a tool on the agent. VERIFY the Send to Story export type and payload key.

agents.name: open_issue
agents.description: SKELETON #49 — POST https://api.github.com/repos/<org>/<repo>/issues with credential github_dispatch (allowed_hosts api.github.com): title, the diagnosis, evidence[], confidence, and an exact `/tines-build-story <slug> "<fix>"` prompt — every model-written string taken from scrub (#79), never from triage.output directly. Labels: ops-finding. Hardened as #8.

payload.title: =CONCAT("[ops] ", verdict.story_name, ": ", scrub.change_summary)
payload.body:
=CONCAT("Finding ", verdict.finding_id, " (severity ", verdict.final_severity, ", confidence ", verdict.confidence, ")

**Hypothesis:** ", scrub.hypothesis, "

**Recommended fix:** ", scrub.recommended_fix, "

**Evidence:**
", JOIN(MAP(scrub.evidence, e → CONCAT("- ", e.source, " ", e.ref, ": ", e.excerpt)), "
"), "

**Prompt:** `/tines-build-story ", DEFAULT(RESOURCE.ops_routing[verdict.story_id].slug, "<slug>"), " "", scrub.recommended_fix, ""`

Requires a PR, lint, an independent review, a human merge and a change-request approval in Tines. Nothing has been changed.")

agents.name: is_auto_pr_kind
agents.description: SKELETON #50 — the target option is on the auto-PR allow-list (retry_on_status, emit_failure_event, a schedule, a DEFAULT() fallback) AND proposals today < ops_limits.max_proposals_per_day (a Records count — sketch).

agents.name: dispatch_fix
agents.description: SKELETON #51 — POST https://api.github.com/repos/<org>/<repo>/dispatches {event_type: tines-fix-proposal, client_payload: the agent's schema output as scrubbed by #79 + finding_id} with credential github_dispatch → propose-fix.yml → /tines-propose-fix → a PR labelled ops-proposal. The pipeline never touches the tenant; the PR still needs lint, review, a human merge, ship.yml and a change-request approval.

agents.name: parse_callback
agents.description: SKELETON #52 — reached only through is_signed_callback (#78): a request Slack signed within the last 5 minutes. JSON_PARSE(slack_callback.body.payload) → actions[0].action_id, actions[0].value ({proposal_id, decision}), user.id, message.ts, channel.id.

agents.name: resolve_user
agents.description: SKELETON #53 — Slack users.info for the clicking user (credential slack_bot; the users:read.email scope — VERIFY) → the email that ops_responders lists. The user id comes from the callback body, so it is trusted only because #77/#78 verified Slack's signature on this request; an unsigned or stale body never reaches this action.

agents.name: load_proposal
agents.description: SKELETON #54 — Records action: the ops_alert_proposals row for proposal_id. The handle is an opaque name; possession is not authorisation.

agents.name: is_verified_approver
agents.description: SKELETON #55 — THE APPROVAL CONTROL: the resolved email is in RESOURCE.ops_responders[proposal.kind]; the proposal is pending; it has not expired; and this email has not already approved it (two approvers must be different people). The button is UI; the Resource is the rule.

rules.path: =INCLUDES(RESOURCE.ops_responders[FIRST(load_proposal.records).kind], resolve_user.body.user.profile.email) AND FIRST(load_proposal.records).status == "pending" AND DATE(FIRST(load_proposal.records).expires_at, "%s") > DATE(NOW(), "%s") AND NOT INCLUDES(DEFAULT(FIRST(load_proposal.records).approver, ""), resolve_user.body.user.profile.email)

agents.name: not_verified
agents.description: SKELETON #56 — the complement of #55 (not an approver, not pending, expired, or a repeat click).

rules.path: =INCLUDES(RESOURCE.ops_responders[FIRST(load_proposal.records).kind], resolve_user.body.user.profile.email) AND FIRST(load_proposal.records).status == "pending" AND DATE(FIRST(load_proposal.records).expires_at, "%s") > DATE(NOW(), "%s") AND NOT INCLUDES(DEFAULT(FIRST(load_proposal.records).approver, ""), resolve_user.body.user.profile.email)

agents.name: deny_callback
agents.description: SKELETON #57 — EXIT. An ephemeral Slack message to the clicker (chat.postEphemeral, credential slack_bot): not an approver for this kind / expired / already approved by you. Nothing changes.

payload.text: =CONCAT("Not applied: you are not listed as an approver for ", FIRST(load_proposal.records).kind, ", or proposal ", parse_callback.proposal_id, " is no longer pending.")

agents.name: is_reject
agents.description: SKELETON #58 — decision == reject.

agents.name: mark_rejected
agents.description: SKELETON #59 — EXIT. Records update: status rejected, approver, at, rejection_reason (the button's reason field, or 'rejected in Slack'). Fed back into the next triage prompt for this story.

agents.name: is_approve
agents.description: SKELETON #60 — decision == approve.

agents.name: needs_second_approval
agents.description: SKELETON #61 — the kind is in ops_responders.two_required_for AND approvals_count < 1 so far (i.e. this is the first click) → record it and wait for a different approver.

agents.name: mark_first_approval
agents.description: SKELETON #62 — EXIT. Records update: approvals_count 1, approver = this email, at. Status stays pending until a second, different approver clicks.

agents.name: is_fully_approved
agents.description: SKELETON #63 — the complement of #61: either one approval suffices for this kind, or this is the second distinct approver.

agents.name: apply
agents.description: SKELETON #64 — Send to Story → [OPS] 16 · Apply approved alert rule (sub) (stories/ops-apply-alert-rule/): THE ONLY PLACE tines_api_ops WRITES TO PRODUCTION, and only here, behind #78, #55 and #63. recipient → POST /api/v1/stories/{id}/recipients (live vs draft VERIFY #7); monitor_* → PUT /api/v1/actions/{id} or PUT /api/v1/stories/{id} into a draft → POST /api/v1/stories/{id}/change_request titled monitor-<finding_id>; token_threshold / credit_budget → Case task or Record + thread [BY HAND]; credit_action (pause / reroute, two approvers) → into a draft + change request only, never live (the action key that pauses an agent is VERIFY — until confirmed, a Record + thread [BY HAND]); disable (two approvers) → NOT a direct POST /disable: it dispatches rollback.yml with emergency: true (credential github_dispatch), so the break-glass job's two GitHub reviewers approve, it disables the named story and appends policies/break-glass-log.md in the same run. Returns {status, change_request_id, message}.

agents.name: mark_applied

Then dead_letter (#76) and release_lock (#74). VERIFY how failure-path links are represented in the export.

local.status: =DEFAULT(live_activity.status, DEFAULT(ai_usage_today.status, DEFAULT(recent_runs.status, DEFAULT(acquire_lock.status, DEFAULT(post_thread.status, DEFAULT(open_issue.status, DEFAULT(dispatch_fix.status, 0)))))))

payload.error_category: =IF(LOCAL.status = 401 OR LOCAL.status = 403, "auth", IF(LOCAL.status = 429, "rate_limit", IF(LOCAL.status >= 500, "upstream_5xx", IF(DEFAULT(triage.meta.VERIFY_schema_valid, true) == false, "schema_failure", "unknown"))))

agents.name: verify_slack_signature
agents.description: SKELETON #77 — THE CALLBACK AUTHENTICATION (between is_callback #6 and parse_callback #52). Slack signs every interactivity request: X-Slack-Signature = 'v0=' + HMAC-SHA256 of 'v0:<X-Slack-Request-Timestamp>:<raw request body>' keyed with the app's signing secret. This transform recomputes it with the Text credential slack_signing_secret and emits only two booleans — never the expected signature, never the secret: signature_valid, and fresh (the timestamp is within 300 s of now, so a captured request cannot be replayed later). Header names reach the story downcased with dashes as underscores (x_slack_signature, x_slack_request_timestamp); slack_callback keeps Include headers ON. VERIFY at build: the formula function names (HMAC_SHA256, ABS), how the Webhook action exposes the raw form-encoded body the signature covers (VERIFY_raw_body), and that a string comparison is acceptable here (no constant-time compare in formulas).

agents.name: is_signed_callback
agents.description: SKELETON #78 — THE GATE: passes only when verify_slack_signature says signature_valid AND fresh. Anything else — a forged block_actions body carrying a listed approver's user id, a replayed request, a missing header — stops here: no parse, no users.info, no Record change, no apply. The approver check (#55) runs only on a request Slack itself signed.

agents.name: scrub
agents.description: SKELETON #79 — THE SECRET SCRUB before anything leaves the tenant (between write_finding #40 and post_thread #41; open_issue #49 and dispatch_fix #51 read it too). Error logs and vendor error bodies are attacker-influenceable and can echo tokens, so every model-written string that is posted to Slack or GitHub — the hypothesis, the recommended fix, the change summary and every evidence excerpt — has each pattern in LOCAL.patterns replaced by [redacted]. LOCAL.patterns mirrors scripts/tines_common.py SECRET_PATTERNS (keep the two in sync in one PR; the header-name entry is spelled so the list itself is not a match). VERIFY at build: the formula function names (REGEX_REPLACE, REDUCE, MAP, MERGE) and regex flavour.

payload.evidence: =MAP(triage.output.evidence, e → {source: LOCAL.clean(e.source), ref: LOCAL.clean(e.ref), excerpt: LOCAL.clean(e.excerpt)})
payload.proposal: =MERGE(triage.output, {root_cause_hypothesis: LOCAL.clean(triage.output.root_cause_hypothesis), recommended_fix: LOCAL.clean(triage.output.recommended_fix), proposed_change: MERGE(triage.output.proposed_change, {summary: LOCAL.clean(triage.output.proposed_change.summary)}), evidence: MAP(triage.output.evidence, e → {source: LOCAL.clean(e.source), ref: LOCAL.clean(e.ref), excerpt: LOCAL.clean(e.excerpt)})})
